title: 32 bits WB cache
body: This PR adapts the WB cache so that it works with the 32 bits versions of CVA6. It was tested using the updated TB from PR #2151 and should also solve the issue #2006. It works by aligning the data to and from the AXI bus on the 64 bits of the bus (lower or upper 32 bits depending on the address).

resolved_issues.title: [BUG] AXI bus trouble with write-back cache
resolved_issues.body:
### Is there an existing CVA6 bug for this?

- [X] I have searched the existing bug issues

### Bug Description

Hi,
I got a SoC project using CVA6 cores, which is running well with its default configuration - cache in write-through mode (config_pkg::WT). I gave a try in write-back mode but without any success. Looking at the AXI bus, I can see some difference while doing the first write access, in an uncachable memory area. Discrepencies are shown hereafter:
![axi_cva6_wt_vs_wb](https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/assets/166120106/1ff00a0d-e224-4351-8890-c6556b2cda3e)
The AXI subsystem acknowledges the access in both situations, but in WB the access seems lost and does not result in an actual access to the target peripheral.

problem_statement:
## Description
In 32-bit CVA6 configurations, the write-back data cache does not correctly format certain uncacheable stores when the AXI data bus is 64 bits wide. A 32-bit store to an uncacheable memory region can be acknowledged on AXI, but the target peripheral still does not observe the write, so the access appears to be lost.

## Expected Behavior
CVA6 must preserve 32-bit store semantics even when the write-back cache interfaces with a 64-bit AXI data bus. For an uncacheable 32-bit store, the request must be forwarded to AXI as a real write to the target peripheral, with the write data and byte strobes placed on the 32-bit lane selected by the address within the 64-bit AXI beat.

## Actual Behavior
With the write-back cache enabled, the AXI-side formatting for these uncacheable 32-bit stores uses the wrong 32-bit lane. As a result, the AXI transaction is acknowledged, but the write data or strobes are misaligned within the 64-bit beat and the intended peripheral write does not occur.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the write-back data-cache control path that converts 32-bit CVA6 memory requests into 64-bit AXI write transactions for uncacheable accesses.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when CVA6 is configured with XLEN=32, the write-back data cache is enabled, the AXI data bus is 64 bits wide, and software performs an uncacheable 32-bit store whose address selects a specific 32-bit lane within the 64-bit AXI beat, including the upper 32-bit half.

resolved_issues.body:
### Is there an existing CVA6 bug for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing bug issues

### Bug Description

Hi @AngelaGonzalezMarino 

I seems to be getting false hit in the shared tlb. 

This condition seems to be suspicious to me:

        if (shared_tag_valid[i] && match_asid && match_vmid && match_stage[i]) begin

@ line 313: 
https://github.com/openhwgroup/cva6/blob/733743da0f9d945e9f6122b50e1050e0f6613d89/core/cva6_mmu/cva6_shared_tlb.sv#L313

I am wondering if we should have    "if (shared_tag_valid[i] && match_asid[i] && match_vmid[i] && match_stage[i])" 

instead of         "if (shared_tag_valid[i] && match_asid && match_vmid && match_stage[i])" begin

We seems to be missing index for match_asid and match_vmid.  Can you please take a look at it ? 

Thanks and Regards
Tanuj Khandelwal

fix_patch:
diff --git a/core/cva6_mmu/cva6_shared_tlb.sv b/core/cva6_mmu/cva6_shared_tlb.sv
index 729d2194c5..9a774ee7e6 100644
--- a/core/cva6_mmu/cva6_shared_tlb.sv
+++ b/core/cva6_mmu/cva6_shared_tlb.sv
@@ -310,7 +310,7 @@ module cva6_shared_tlb #(
         // check if translation is a: S-Stage and G-Stage, S-Stage only or G-Stage only translation and virtualization mode is on/off
         match_stage[i] = shared_tag_rd[i].v_st_enbl == v_st_enbl[i_req_q][HYP_EXT*2:0];
 
-        if (shared_tag_valid[i] && match_asid && match_vmid && match_stage[i]) begin
+        if (shared_tag_valid[i] && match_asid[i] && match_vmid[i] && match_stage[i]) begin
           if (|level_match[i]) begin
             shared_tlb_hit_d = 1'b1;
             if (itlb_req_q) begin
problem_statement:
## Description
CVA6 uses a shared translation lookaside buffer (shared TLB) to cache page translations and refill the instruction and data TLBs. The shared TLB lookup can report a hit even when no single cached entry matches the entire request. If one way in a set matches the requested virtual page and a different way matches the requested address-space identifier (ASID), the lookup can incorrectly treat that as a valid hit and return a translation from the wrong address space.

## Expected Behavior
A shared TLB hit is valid only when one cached entry matches all lookup fields for the current request. At minimum, the requested virtual page and the ASID must match in the same entry; if additional virtualization qualifiers are enabled for that translation context, those qualifiers must also match in that same entry. If no single entry satisfies the full lookup, the shared TLB must miss so that CVA6 refills the instruction or data TLB from the correct translation.

## Actual Behavior
The lookup can combine partial matches from different ways in the same set and report a false hit. As a result, CVA6 can return a cached translation even though the ASID of the request does not match the entry that supplied the translation.

## Affected Functionality
Shared TLB hit-detection and tag-match logic in the CVA6 memory-management unit (MMU), specifically the logic that decides whether a cached translation can be used to refill the instruction-side or data-side TLB.

## Trigger Condition
The bug appears when a shared-TLB set contains multiple valid entries with different ASIDs. A concrete failing case is: one way holds virtual page X for ASID 0, another way in the same set holds a different virtual page for ASID 1, and a lookup is performed for virtual page X under ASID 1. That lookup must miss because no single entry matches both X and ASID 1, but the buggy logic can report a hit.

problem_statement:
## Description
In CVA6, the memory management unit (MMU) translates virtual addresses for load and store requests from the load/store unit (LSU). When an LSU request already carries a valid misaligned-address exception, that request should be treated as faulting immediately. Instead, the load/store translation path can still start data-side address translation and produce a page-table memory access for the same request.

## Expected Behavior
If the LSU presents a load or store together with a valid misaligned-address exception, the MMU must return the misaligned exception for that access and stop the translation flow for that request. The same access must not trigger a data-side translation lookup or any page-table memory request.

## Actual Behavior
With load/store address translation enabled, a misaligned LSU request can still initiate translation-side activity and generate an observable page-table memory access even though the request is already being reported as misaligned.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the MMU load/store address-translation path, specifically the gating between LSU requests that already carry an exception and the data-side translation/page-table access path.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when load/store virtual-address translation is enabled and the LSU submits a load or store request that already has a valid misaligned-address exception.

title: Fix a bug that causes the core to freeze when enabling CV-X-IF while disabling RVC extension
body:
This is an attempt to fix the bug described in #3167.

It appears that when enabling the CV-X-IF interface while disabling the RVC extension, the core freezes during the initialization phase of the debug sequence in the testbench.

I managed to find out that this was caused by a bug inside the Decode stage: the compressed‑instruction channel driver of the CV-X-IF inside the Decode stage is only generated if the RVC extension is enabled. However, this module still drives signals inside the stage even when RVC is off. I proposed a fix in the PR below, although I am not sure it is the cleanest way to address the issue.

problem_statement:
## Description
CVA6 can lose forward progress when the CV-X-IF interface for custom extensions is enabled while the RVC extension, the RISC-V compressed-instruction extension, is disabled. In this configuration, the Decode stage can still let the CV-X-IF compressed-instruction path affect instruction decoding even though compressed instructions are not supported. The failure was observed during debug-sequence initialization, where the core freezes instead of continuing execution.

## Expected Behavior
When RVC is disabled, a fetched instruction must be handled as a normal 32-bit uncompressed instruction. Enabling CV-X-IF in that configuration must not block decode, prevent a valid decode result from being issued, change the forwarded 32-bit instruction value, or mark the instruction as compressed.

## Actual Behavior
With CV-X-IF enabled and RVC disabled, the Decode stage may incorrectly let the compressed-instruction path participate in decode. As a result, an ordinary 32-bit instruction can fail to produce a valid issued decode result or be treated as compressed, which causes the core to stop making forward progress.

## Affected Function
Decode-stage handling of the interaction between the normal instruction-decode path and the CV-X-IF compressed-instruction path.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when CV-X-IF is enabled in a CVA6 configuration that disables RVC, and the core decodes a regular 32-bit instruction, including early instructions seen during debug-sequence initialization.
